title: Miso Turkey Burgers
changes_from_base: Turkey thigh is part-frozen and ground at home in a food processor, then seasoned with a little miso for a deeper, beefier flavour; the burgers are browned hard on one side and finished gently under a lid ajar.
summary: Turkey thighs pulsed to a fine texture and seasoned with umami-rich white miso make tender, juicy burgers with crispy golden exteriors.
equipment: large heavy frying pan with a lid

ingredients.item: boneless, skinless turkey thighs, cut into 2-3 cm chunks
fine sea salt or table salt
white miso paste, loosened with 2 tsp water

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Spread 680 g turkey thigh chunks on a baking tray and freeze for about 30 minutes until they are firm at the edges.

steps.title: Process
steps.text: Pulse the chilled turkey in a food processor in 3 separate batches, using 12-14 short pulses each, until no piece is larger than about 3 mm; this creates a finer texture than mincing alone.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Tip the processed turkey into a bowl and gently mix with ½ tsp fine salt, ½ tsp ground black pepper and 2 tsp white miso paste that has been loosened with 2 tsp water. Divide the mixture into 4 equal portions and shape each gently into a patty about 2.5 cm thick.

steps.title: Sear
steps.text: Heat a large heavy frying pan over a medium heat for 4-5 minutes until very hot, then add 15 ml vegetable oil followed by the patties, spacing them apart. Cook without moving them for about 5 minutes until the undersides are dark brown and crusty.

steps.title: Cook through
steps.text: Turn the patties and cook for another 4-5 minutes until lightly browned on the second side, then lower the heat and place the lid on the pan ajar. Continue cooking for 5-6 minutes more until the thickest part of each patty reaches 74 °C when checked with a thermometer.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Transfer the burgers to toasted buns and serve at once with fresh lettuce leaves and sliced tomato.

tips: Freeze the turkey chunks briefly to make them easier to pulse into a consistent fine texture without overworking the meat.
Keep the pan lid slightly ajar during the final cooking stage so steam escapes gently and the patties cook through without drying out.
Use a meat thermometer to check the centre reaches 74 °C, ensuring the turkey is fully cooked but still moist inside.
storage: Best served immediately whilst the burgers are still warm and tender. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
